title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

reading.body:
This is an insider misuse case, not a model failure. A person with authorised access to law enforcement systems is accused of using them for a purpose they were not deployed for: personal tracking. The systems named are a sheriff's office camera network, a tag reader network, and a state crime database, all built and operated for investigative work. The failure sits at the point of access, where legitimate credentials meet a personal motive, and no technical control described in the reporting is said to have stopped it.

Catching this kind of misuse is a logging and audit problem rather than a model problem. The relevant question is whether queries and lookups made by an account are reviewed against the case or duty that justifies them, and whether a pattern of searches unrelated to that person's assignments surfaces to a supervisor. The reporting does not say what oversight existed, whether any audit flagged the activity, or how the conduct came to light.

What is established is an indictment, which is an allegation, not a finding of guilt. Rozar was terminated when the investigation began, arrested on May 5, and released on bond the same day, with arraignment scheduled for May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court. The reporting does not establish his intent, the outcome of the case, or whether the systems involved had any access controls beyond standard credentials.

reports.title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

summary:
A former Coffee County deputy, Chris Ashley Rozar, was released on bond after a grand jury indicted him on eight counts, including stalking and misuse of law enforcement databases. The 49-year-old is accused of using the sheriff's office camera system, tag reader system, and a state crime database for personal reasons between April and May 2024. He was terminated when the investigation began.

The woman he allegedly tracked spoke anonymously, saying she hopes her story helps other women report abuse. Rozar was arrested on May 5 and released on bond the same day. He is scheduled for arraignment on May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court. The Georgia Bureau of Investigation led the multi-year investigation.
